newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/15.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 14.0/15.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged up slightly to 14.0/15.0 percent on Tuesday morning from 13.0/14.0 at the opening, dealers said.
They said rupiah supply appeared to be adequate despite initial fears of a possible squeeze since tax payments at mid-month were usually larger than usual.
Bank Indonesia supplied 300 billion rupiah into the market.
One state bank dealer said operators were not panicky because they still can settle tax payments on Friday.
Another state bank dealer said he anticipated further easing in the afternoon as tax payments on Tuesday were moderate and could increase on Friday.
One local bank dealer said operators remained cautious because some operators with funds were holding back to cash in on possible higher interbank rates.
He said longer-term rates remained firm, with one-week money quoted at 13.50/13.75 and one-month at 13.5/13.625 percent.
The central bank kept its bilateral rates unchanged, with one-week bilateral papers (SBIs) at 6.5 percent, two-week at 8.5 percent, one- and three-month at 10.25 and 11.25 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 14.26 percent. compared with 10.13 percent last Friday.
Bond dealers said prices were stable, with the focus on new bond issues. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
